subject: biology
title: Cell Cycle & Division Adventure
welcome_lead: Today you'll trace the cell cycle and the stages of mitosis and meiosis.
meta_desc: A-Level Biology Cells — G1, S, G2, M phases, PMAT of mitosis, and meiosis with independent assortment and crossing over.
final_note: You learned that the cell cycle has G1, S, G2 and M phases, mitosis produces 2 identical diploid cells, and meiosis produces 4 genetically different haploid gametes.

DNA replication — each chromosome becomes 2 sister chromatids
Further growth and checkpoint before mitosis

walkthroughs.body_html:
Most of a cell's life is spent in interphase.

Stages:
- G1 — growth, organelles duplicate
- S — DNA replicates (chromosome → 2 chromatids)
- G2 — final growth, checkpoint
- M — mitosis + cytokinesis

Checkpoints prevent damaged DNA being copied. Loss of control → tumours.

Prophase — chromosomes condense, nuclear envelope breaks down, spindle forms.
Metaphase — chromosomes line up at the equator.
Anaphase — sister chromatids pulled to opposite poles.
Telophase — chromosomes decondense, nuclear envelope reforms.

Result: 2 diploid cells, genetically identical to the parent. Used for growth, repair, asexual reproduction.

Two divisions: meiosis I separates homologous pairs; meiosis II separates sister chromatids.

Final result: 4 haploid gametes, each genetically unique.

Two variation sources:
- Independent assortment — random arrangement at metaphase I (2²³ combinations in humans)
- Crossing over — chromatids exchange segments at chiasmata in prophase I

Plus random fertilisation → essentially infinite variety.

mcqs.q: What is the key difference between mitosis and meiosis?
options: Mitosis produces two genetically identical diploid cells; meiosis produces four genetically different haploid cells (gametes).
Mitosis and meiosis both produce gametes; they are basically the same.
Mitosis happens in plants and meiosis happens in animals.
Prokaryotes are always smaller than 1 micrometre and have no cytoplasm.

Prokaryotes have no DNA — that's why they have no nucleus.
Mitosis happens in plants and meiosis happens in animals.
Eukaryotes have a membrane-bound nucleus and membrane-bound organelles; prokaryotes do not.
Stem cells are simply cells that haven't grown big enough yet.
Prokaryotes are always smaller than 1 micrometre and have no cytoplasm.
Stem cells are taken only from embryos and cannot be found in adults.
An undifferentiated cell capable of dividing to produce more stem cells or differentiating into specialised cell types.
